stem.text: A particle moves along the x-axis. Its position at time t seconds is \( x(t) = t^{3} + 2 t^{2} - 12 t - 6 \) meters, for \( t \ge 0 \). Find the speed of the particle at time t = 1, and determine whether the speed is increasing or decreasing at that time. Give a reason for the answer.

answer_key.label: The speed is 5 meters per second, and it is decreasing at that time, because \( v(1) = -5 \) and \( a(1) = 10 \) have opposite signs.

worked_solution.text: Velocity is the derivative of position, \( v(t) = 3 t^{2} + 4 t - 12 \), so \( v(1) = -5 \).
worked_solution.rule_named: velocity is the derivative of position

worked_solution.text: Acceleration is the derivative of velocity, \( a(t) = 6 t + 4 \), so \( a(1) = 10 \).
worked_solution.rule_named: acceleration is the derivative of velocity

worked_solution.text: The speed is \( \left|v(1)\right| = 5 \) meters per second.
worked_solution.rule_named: speed is the absolute value of velocity

worked_solution.text: Because \( v(1) = -5 \) and \( a(1) = 10 \) have opposite signs, the speed of the particle is decreasing at t = 1.
worked_solution.rule_named: speed increases when velocity and acceleration share a sign

options.derivation: the speed reported as the signed velocity
